original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant C > 0 such that every (n, d, lambda')-graph with d/lambda' >= C contains a Hamilton cycle?
target_in_paper: Section 8, Conjecture 9 (Krivelevich-Sudakov), in the topic “Hamilton cycles in pseudo-random graphs.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s intended target very closely: it asks for an absolute constant C > 0, quantifies over every (n, d, λ′)-graph, uses the ratio d/λ′, and asks whether such a graph must contain a Hamilton cycle. That is exactly the content of Section 8, Conjecture 9. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
missing_details: To make the question stand-alone, you should define an (n, d, λ′)-graph explicitly: it is a d-regular graph G on n vertices whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue in absolute value is at most λ′. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
You should make clear that λ′ is an adjacency-spectrum parameter, not a Laplacian parameter. This is part of the local notation in Section 8. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))

The paper works throughout with graphs that are simple, undirected, and unweighted; if you want the question to be fully paper-faithful and self-contained, those ambient assumptions should be stated. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
It helps to spell out that the constant C is absolute, i.e. independent of n, d, and λ′. This is implicit in the paper’s wording. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))

You should not add any asymptotic qualifier such as “for all sufficiently large n”: in Section 8 that phrase appears only in the discussion of partial results, not in Conjecture 9 itself. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
refined_question: Does there exist an absolute constant C > 0 such that every simple, undirected, unweighted d-regular graph G on n vertices whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue in absolute value is at most λ′—that is, every (n, d, λ′)-graph—with d/λ′ ≥ C contains a Hamilton cycle? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
justification: The draft is trying to capture the paper’s Krivelevich-Sudakov conjecture in Section 8, and it already reproduces the main mathematical content almost verbatim. The nearby context in Section 8 supplies the only missing stand-alone information, namely the definition of an (n, d, λ′)-graph and the fact that λ′ refers to the second largest adjacency eigenvalue in absolute value. The paper’s global setup also fixes the ambient graph class as simple, undirected, and unweighted. Finally, the discussion immediately after Conjecture 9 shows that “for sufficiently large n” belongs to earlier partial theorems, not to the conjecture itself. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2305.10290))
